title: MINI-CHALLENGE: Complete Boot Diagnostic

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Now integrate everything: sequential messages, severity levels, dual channels, and proper structure. Create a complete boot diagnostic that would make any senior robot proud."
story.requirements: Build a comprehensive diagnostic that uses all four file sections and demonstrates Robot Framework's flexibility while following best practices.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Outstanding! That's a professional-grade boot diagnostic. You've mastered basic communication. Now let's move deeper—into data and memory."

description: Create a complete, professional boot diagnostic system that integrates ALL Section 1.1 concepts: file structure, sequential execution, log levels, dual channels, and syntax flexibility.
requirements: Use all four file sections: Settings, Variables, Test Cases, Keywords
Create a comprehensive boot sequence test with 8-10 sequential steps
Use multiple log levels (INFO, WARN, ERROR) appropriately
Use both Log and Log To Console for dual-channel output
Define and use at least 2 variables (ship name, status)
Demonstrate at least one syntax flexibility feature (case variation or spacing variation)
Include proper documentation in Settings section
constraints: All sections must be present and properly formatted
Minimum 8 log statements across all severity levels
At least 3 Log To Console statements for progress tracking
Variables must be used in at least one log message
Custom keyword must be called from the test case
One keyword must demonstrate case or spacing flexibility
instructions: Create '*** Settings ***' section with Documentation: 'Complete ship boot diagnostic system'
Create '*** Test Cases ***' section with test named 'Complete Boot Diagnostic'
Start test with: Log To Console 'Starting boot diagnostic for ${SHIP_NAME}...'
Log 8-10 sequential boot stages using INFO, WARN, and ERROR levels (core systems, memory, protocols, sensors, navigation, communications, hull)
Intersperse 4 progress updates: Log To Console '25% complete', '50% complete', '75% complete', '100% complete'
Demonstrate syntax flexibility: use 'log' (lowercase) OR 'LOG' (uppercase) for ONE Log statement
Call custom keyword 'Generate Boot Summary' at the end of the test
Create '*** Keywords ***' section with keyword 'Generate Boot Summary'
Inside 'Generate Boot Summary': Log 'Boot diagnostic complete for ${SHIP_NAME} - Version ${BOOT_VERSION}'
Inside 'Generate Boot Summary': Log To Console 'All systems analyzed - Review report for details'
hints: Remember: all four sections must be present
Use ${SHIP_NAME} and ${BOOT_VERSION} in your log messages
Mix Log and Log To Console appropriately (console for progress, log for details)
INFO for normal operations, WARN for concerns, ERROR for critical issues
Custom keywords are defined in *** Keywords *** section and called like regular keywords
Demonstrate flexibility by using 'log' or 'LOG' instead of 'Log' for ONE statement
Progress updates (25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) should go to console
Don't forget to call your custom keyword from the test case
solution:
*** Settings ***
Documentation    Complete ship boot diagnostic system

*** Variables ***
${SHIP_NAME}        Starlight Explorer
${BOOT_VERSION}     7.2.1
${STATUS}           Initializing

*** Test Cases ***
Complete Boot Diagnostic
    Log To Console    Starting boot diagnostic for ${SHIP_NAME}...
    Log    Initializing core systems...    INFO
    Log    Memory banks: 47/48 operational    INFO
    Log To Console    Progress: 25% complete
    Log    Loading diagnostic protocols version ${BOOT_VERSION}    INFO
    log    Sensor array calibration: 2 sensors offline    WARN
    Log To Console    Progress: 50% complete
    Log    Navigation systems: Online    INFO
    Log    Communication array: Primary antenna damaged    ERROR
    Log To Console    Progress: 75% complete
    Log    Hull integrity: Minor breaches detected    WARN
    Log    Boot sequence analysis complete    INFO
    Log To Console    Progress: 100% complete
    Generate Boot Summary

*** Keywords ***
Generate Boot Summary
    Log    Boot diagnostic complete for ${SHIP_NAME} - Version ${BOOT_VERSION}
    Log To Console    All systems analyzed - Review report for details

theory.title: Section 1.1 Mini-Challenge: Integration and Mastery
theory.content:
\n\n
\n\n

MENTOR-9 brings up a large holographic checklist. Each item represents a concept you've learned in Section 1.1.

"PROTO-7, you've learned the pieces. Now show me you can build something complete. A real diagnostic system that any ship engineer would trust."

What This Challenge Tests

ConceptWhere It AppearsWhy It Matters
File Structure All four sections Professional tests are organized, not chaotic
Sequential Execution 8-10 log statements in order Complex workflows require multiple ordered steps
Log Levels INFO/WARN/ERROR mix Severity helps prioritize what to fix first
Dual Channels Log + Log To Console Real-time progress + detailed records
Variables ${SHIP_NAME}, ${BOOT_VERSION} Reusable data makes tests maintainable
Custom Keywords Generate Boot Summary Reusability and abstraction
Syntax Flexibility log vs Log variation Understanding what's allowed vs preferred

Real-World Application

This challenge mirrors actual test automation scenarios:

  • System startup tests - Verify applications boot correctly
  • Health checks - Monitor multiple service components
  • Integration tests - Check system-wide functionality
  • Diagnostic suites - Comprehensive status reporting

Professional Patterns You're Implementing:

1. Separation of Concerns
  • Settings: Configuration and metadata
  • Variables: Test data
  • Test Cases: The actual tests
  • Keywords: Reusable helper functions
2. Progress Communication
Log To Console    Progress: 25% complete
Log    Detailed step information...
Log To Console    Progress: 50% complete

Users see progress in real-time, details are logged for later.

3. Severity-Based Reporting

At a glance, engineers know:

  • ✅ What's working (INFO)
  • ⚠️ What needs attention (WARN)
  • ❌ What's critical (ERROR)
4. Data Reusability
*** Variables ***
${SHIP_NAME}    Starlight Explorer

*** Test Cases ***
Boot Test
    Log    Starting ${SHIP_NAME} boot...
    Log    ${SHIP_NAME} boot complete!

Change the ship name once, it updates everywhere. This is maintainability.

Success Criteria

Your diagnostic is successful if:

  1. ✅ All four sections present and properly formatted
  2. ✅ Variables used in log messages
  3. ✅ Multiple log levels appropriately chosen
  4. ✅ Console shows progress, log shows details
  5. ✅ Custom keyword defined and called
  6. ✅ At least one syntax flexibility demonstration
  7. ✅ Test passes without errors
  8. ✅ Output is clear, professional, and informative

MENTOR-9 steps back, arms crossed. "This is your first real test, PROTO-7. Build a diagnostic system that proves you understand Robot Framework fundamentals. Show me what you've learned."

"If this diagnostic is good, we move to advanced topics. If it's lacking... we review the basics."

She nods toward the editor. "Begin."
